# Natural landmark and Treasure Cove assets

Original geometry for this project, authored 2026-09-15. These are architectural interpretations from public visual references, not measured scans or official Disney 3D assets.

## Runtime files

| File | Dimensions X × Y × Z in metres | Triangles | Meshes | Size |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| roaring-mountain.glb | 88.56 × 36.45 × 71.63 | 238,380 | 11 | 8,592,328 bytes |
| treasure-cove-port.glb | 89.93 × 15.80 × 36.79 | 37,298 | 10 | 2,328,544 bytes |
| treasure-cove-galleon.glb | 12.50 × 28.25 × 37.05 | 108,322 | 12 | 3,558,672 bytes |

All models are Y-up, metre units. The origin is the horizontal centre of the entire asset at its lowest point (ground Y=0). +Z faces the mountain waterfalls, port waterfront, or ship bow. Mount and port ground elevations include their base features. Place the galleon keel at the appropriate water depth; its hull is included below deck. Apply uniform scale only if adapting the visual estimate.

GLB embeds all textures. Required extension: KHR_mesh_quantization, supported by Three.js GLTFLoader. No Draco, Meshopt, external texture, external buffer, or other decoder dependency. MikkTSpace tangents included for every normal-mapped material. JPEGs are embedded at up to 1024px. Geometry was welded/quantized, never simplified.

## Content and scope

- Mountain: irregular volumetric cliff/mesa masses with procedural fractures and stratification, summit caps, multiple smaller outcrops, waterfall channels, low river loop, original temple terrace, hiking bridge, rope rails and sparse low vegetation.
- Port: sea-fort bastions and gate, five differentiated waterfront buildings, tiled roofs, arcades, shuttered windows, balconies, detailed doors, quays, three piers, mooring ropes, barrels/crates and cannon.
- Galleon: curved hull and trim, gun ports, planked decks, aft cabins/balcony, stern ornament, three masts, spars, crow nests, nine billowed sails with seams, stays, shrouds/ratlines, bowsprit, cannon, capstan, hatches and stairs. Flags have no borrowed emblems.

The approximately 35m mountain height is a visual scale estimate: the official references consulted do not publish a measured mountain height. The 36.45m final bbox includes the sculpted crest. Port width and ship dimensions are design estimates suitable for whole-park placement. The port represents the visible waterfront facade collection, not the approximately 157 × 159m Pirates backstage/showbuilding footprint. The temple and minor facade/rigging detail are original plausible architectural details, not claims of exact as-built replication.

## Sources and licensing

### Embedded third-party surface material

- **Rock Face** by Dario Barresi (processing) and Greg Zaal (photography), Poly Haven.
  - Asset: https://polyhaven.com/a/rock_face
  - License: CC0-1.0, https://polyhaven.com/license
  - File metadata: https://api.polyhaven.com/files/rock_face (saved in rock-face-files.json).
  - Embedded maps: 1K diffuse, OpenGL normal, roughness; diffuse desaturated and brightened for the mountain interpretation. The original surface width is listed as 2.4m; UV tiling on the interpretation is artistic.
  - The downloaded displacement map is working material only; actual macro rock displacement is original generated geometry.

All other textures are original procedural canvas materials generated by build-assets.js. All mesh geometry is original and contains no third-party source mesh. No additional third-party licensing obligations attach to those original components.

## Validation and reproducibility

- Each *-validation.json is a Khronos glTF Validator report: all three exports pass with zero errors and zero warnings.
- runtime-validation.json records final optimized GLB loads and texture decoding in Three.js/Edge, bounding boxes and WebGL state.
- *-final.png previews render the final optimized GLBs, not only the generator scene.
- build-assets.js contains the model source. Run work/asset-tools/build-natural.mjs from work/asset-tools, then optimize-natural.mjs with the three model base names, then verify-natural.mjs.
- build-report.json is the pre-optimization generator report; final file sizes above and final bbox values in runtime-validation.json are authoritative.
